reviews.checked_passages: Section 2.2 printed pp.11–13: type-counting bounds, Definition2.9 of finite order patterns/stability, Proposition2.10 and the Erdos–Makkai combinatorial argument in Theorem2.13. Section2.4 printed pp.16–19 was inspected for indiscernibility definitions, the Ramsey/compactness construction, and scope boundaries.
reviews.consumers: [Indiscernible sequences](entries/indiscernible-sequences/entry.html) and [Order patterns and stability](entries/order-patterns-and-stability/entry.html). The latter adopts Definitions2.9/Proposition2.10 and gives explicit cut/equality type counts; the Erdos–Makkai proof was inspected for scope but is not adopted in this introduction.
reviews.outcome: CHERNIKOV-ST-01 records the missing distinctness hypothesis in adjacent Lemma2.31. The corpus will require an infinite source for Ramsey extraction, distinguish a newly constructed sequence from a subsequence, and avoid monster-model assumptions in the elementary compactness construction. Later spectra, forking, ranks, and the full characterization theorem are outside the adopted scope. Theorem2.37 and its compressed pattern-selection step were not adopted or certified.

reviews.checked_passages: Section2.2 Definition2.3 and Exercise2.4, printed p11, and the use of that exercise at the end of Proposition2.10, p12; statement/hint inspection, reusing the earlier broader section2.2 assessment.
reviews.consumers: First-four-foundational-area gap audit; proposed coverage only, with no new entry adoption.
reviews.outcome: Exercise2.4 confirms the missing finite-tuple-to-one-variable type-counting bridge. The source leaves it as an exercise, so a corpus treatment must supply the transport and induction argument rather than cite it as an already explained proof. Full stability equivalence, spectra, ranks and forking are not newly audited.

reviews.checked_passages: Adoption reuses section2.2 Definition2.3 and Exercise2.4, printed p11, with its application on p12, from the scoped Nov12 statement/hint inspection.
reviews.outcome: The source leaves the finite-tuple bound as an exercise. The corpus supplies the full prefix/tail transport, a fixed small model for each prefix, a tail-type injection and finite-length cardinal induction. Existing strongly minimal one-type bounds then yield smallness and countable saturated/prime models. No new adoption of the full no-order-property equivalence, stability spectrum, ranks or forking.
